title: Old parks and the gardeners' picnic at Southern Park
summary: Allen asks about Crescent Pleasure Park, Southern Park and others; Stecklet recalls the gardeners' picnic and a tomato-growing prize winner.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I wanted to ask about a few of the parks. We'll ask you in a minute about Millenburg too. But I have a name, some names of some real old parks here. The Crescent Pleasure Park. Do you remember that? Crescent Pleasure Park. It said it was next to the Oakland Park, which was out at the near Metry Road, on the Shell Road. Do you remember Oakland? No. Riding Park. That was the riding park. No, I don't. I don't know if they had races or what they had there. No, I don't know nothing about that. That must have been up in Jefferson Parish. Yes, out in Metry, I suppose. Yeah, that's Jefferson Parish. There's a few other parks here I was going to ask. Southern Park. Oh, yes.
Oh, yeah, that was back there. By St. John. Back along by St. John. Southern Park.
Yes, all the picnics and everything out there. So they have music there too?

Oh, yeah, they used to have a regular lay there. Because the gardeners used to give a picnic there. And when the young girls, their daughter would be, you know, sitting down there, and the fellow would come along, he'd top them on the show and tell them, dance with my daughter and I'll give you a quarter. Yeah. To get them to dance with some of them girls. Then they had at the gardeners picnic, they had a fellow every year. He used to win the best prize on tomatoes. You see? Of course, it was open to all the vegetable growers to enter the best that they could raise and show it. And they'd win the prize on them. So this old brother, I can't think of his name anymore. But every year he used to win the first prize on tomatoes. So I was doing some work down near his place. And I said to him, his name is Mark.

might come to me later. I said to him, you must have some device that you, or something that you pump in those tomatoes to make them develop so big. I said, can't you tell the fella the name? He says, that's what all of them gardeners is trying to find out. He says, I know I got that laid up every year that I'm going to win the first prize on tomatoes.
